about: Twelve laws/theorems to scout for papers and data across plants, animals and the fossil record. Claim ids are in docs/claims.json. Slices are law x kingdom; 'fossils' covers fossil plants and fossil animals. Scouting only: nothing here runs a test.

providers.rule: Law i is scouted by rotation[i % 4]; its remediation rounds 2, 4, 5 use rotation[(i+1) % 4], [(i+2) % 4], [(i+3) % 4]. Four different providers per law; the scout never audits its own work.

laws.title: Horns, shells, claws and teeth are logarithmic spirals
variables: growth ratio or spiral pitch angle per specimen (Raup W, D, T; or log-spiral fit parameters)
specimen outline, image or CT scan
taxon and body part

kingdoms.plants: coiled tendrils, fern fiddleheads, spiral seed pods and pollen-tube or root coils, spiral algae; sources that fit a spiral to a plant organ
kingdoms.animals: mollusc shells (nautilus, snails), bovid and other horns, beaks, claws, teeth, tusks, cochlea; shell-coiling datasets (Raup, Okamoto, Urdy, Hammer), morphometric image archives
kingdoms.fossils: ammonoids, nautiloids, gastropods, brachiopods, foraminifera, fossil horns and tusks; PBDB occurrence plus coiling parameters; MorphoSource or Dryad scans

laws.title: Fibonacci phyllotaxis: one parastichy pair entails all lower pairs
variables: parastichy pair (m, n) or divergence angle per organism
leaves or organs per turn of the genetic spiral
species and organ (cone, capitulum, shoot, rosette)

kingdoms.plants: surveys of parastichy numbers and divergence angles across species and organ types (cones, sunflower heads, cacti, succulents, shoots); meristem imaging datasets; non-Fibonacci and anomalous cases too
kingdoms.animals: spiral or Fibonacci arrangements outside plants (coral polyps, sponge or bryozoan zooids, feather and scale placement, Volvox-like colonies); say plainly when the animal side is thin
kingdoms.fossils: leaf cushions and scars (Lepidodendron, Sigillaria, Calamites), fossil cones, cycadeoids, crinoid and echinoderm plate spirals; counts of parastichies from fossil specimens

laws.title: Optimal branching: cube law, branch angle and wall thickness follow a flow-cost law
variables: parent and daughter vessel radii at junctions
branch angles at junctions
vessel wall thickness against radius or pressure

kingdoms.plants: leaf venation, xylem vessel and root branching networks, with measured junction radii or angles (Murray's law in plants, leaf vein networks, hydraulic architecture datasets)
kingdoms.animals: arterial and venous trees, airways, insect tracheae, vascular corrosion casts, retinal vessels, sponge canals; published junction radius and angle tables
kingdoms.fossils: fossil leaf venation (cleared-leaf collections, Cretaceous angiosperms), fossil bone vascular canals, fossil root systems, fossil sponge or coral canal systems

laws.title: Plateau 120-degree cell-wall junctions and hexagonal packing
variables: wall junction angles
neighbour counts or polygon-class distribution per cell
cell area distribution
segmented tissue images

kingdoms.plants: leaf and root epidermis, shoot apical meristem, parenchyma and cork sections; segmented cell-network datasets (e.g. confocal meristem atlases)
kingdoms.animals: epithelia (Drosophila wing disc and pupal wing, Hydra, cornea, retina), honeycomb and insect cells, ommatidia; neighbour-count (Lewis law) datasets; wing venation networks
kingdoms.fossils: cellularly preserved tissue (Rhynie chert, fossil wood and cork, silicified plants), fossil bee comb or wasp nests, foraminifera or bryozoan packing

laws.title: Turing pattern wavelength is set by reaction and diffusion, not tissue size
variables: pattern spacing or wavelength per individual
tissue or domain size
perturbation of diffusion or reaction parameters
pattern images

kingdoms.plants: stomatal, trichome, root-hair and leaf-pattern spacing; Arabidopsis patterning mutants; experimental and modelled wavelength vs domain size
kingdoms.animals: zebrafish and other fish stripes, mouse digits and palatal rugae, feather and hair follicle spacing, felid coats, chameleon and lizard skin; wavelength vs body size or perturbation experiments
kingdoms.fossils: fossil skin, feather and colour patterns (pigment preservation), fossil digit and rugae counts, stromatolite and trace-fossil spacing; say plainly when thin

laws.title: Weight varies as the cube of length; a change in k means a change of form
variables: body or organism mass and length per individual or species
reported exponent b and condition factor k
age or size class

kingdoms.plants: stem, trunk and shoot biomass against height or diameter; allometry databases (BAAD, Tallo, GlobAllomeTree), seed and leaf mass vs dimension
kingdoms.animals: length-weight relationships (FishBase LWR, bird and mammal body-mass tables, AnAge, PanTHERIA, Amniote database), growth series with measured L and W
kingdoms.fossils: body-mass estimates from fossil length (dinosaur, fish, mammal compilations), measured fossil lengths with mass proxies, volumetric reconstructions

laws.title: Scaling limits: tree diameter ~ height^(3/2); gravity caps terrestrial size
variables: tree height and trunk diameter per tree
limb-bone circumference or cross-section against body mass
maximum body mass of land animals

kingdoms.plants: tree height-diameter datasets (Tallo, global forest inventories, giant-tree records), elastic-similarity and buckling studies
kingdoms.animals: limb-bone scaling (Biewener, Alexander, Campione & Evans), muscle cross-section vs mass, maximum size of land animals, mammal and bird body-mass databases
kingdoms.fossils: sauropod, proboscidean and other fossil limb dimensions with mass estimates, Carboniferous giant arthropods and trees, maximum body size through time

laws.title: Wolff's law: trabeculae and cortical wall thickness follow stress and bending moment
variables: trabecular orientation or fabric tensor per bone region
cortical wall thickness along the shaft
loading or principal stress direction
micro-CT volumes

kingdoms.plants: stem and trunk wood grain or reaction wood following mechanical stress, thigmomorphogenesis, tree-ring and fibre-orientation datasets; say plainly when thin
kingdoms.animals: micro-CT of femora, humeri and vertebrae across species (MorphoSource, Dryad, Zenodo), trabecular-orientation and bone-ecology databases, finite-element comparisons
kingdoms.fossils: CT scans of dinosaur, synapsid and hominin trabecular and cortical bone, fossil bone histology, fossil femur cross-sections

laws.title: Neutral substitution rate equals the mutation rate (the molecular clock)
variables: per-generation mutation rate per lineage
substitution rate or divergence between lineages
divergence time from fossil calibration
generation time and effective population size

kingdoms.plants: plant mutation-rate and substitution-rate studies (Arabidopsis, rice, Oenothera), plant divergence-time calibrations and genomes
kingdoms.animals: pedigree and mutation-accumulation rate compilations (e.g. Bergeron et al.), vertebrate and insect genomes, TimeTree divergence estimates
kingdoms.fossils: fossil calibration databases and fossil-calibrated trees (Fossil Calibration Database, PBDB first appearances, node-dating compilations)

laws.title: Fisher-KPP: an advantageous gene or population advances as a wave of fixed speed
variables: front position through time or space
dispersal kernel or diffusion coefficient
growth rate or selection coefficient
range-edge occurrence records

kingdoms.plants: post-glacial tree migration from pollen (Neotoma), invasive plant spread rates, allele or herbicide-resistance spread
kingdoms.animals: invasion fronts (cane toad, muskrat, collared dove, starling), range expansions, allele-frequency clines and sweeps with spatial data, GBIF time-stamped occurrences
kingdoms.fossils: fossil range shifts and Holocene or Pleistocene expansions, PBDB/Neotoma time series of first occurrences along transects, migration-rate estimates

laws.title: Speed varies as the square root of linear size in swimming, flight and walking
variables: measured speed per species or individual
body length per species
locomotion mode

kingdoms.animals: fish swimming speed, bird flight speed, walking and running speed (Froude number), Alexander and Hoyt-type compilations, tracked-animal speed datasets (Movebank, FishBase swimming)
kingdoms.fossils: speeds inferred from trackways (dinosaur, early tetrapod, arthropod), stride length with limb length, fossil fish and flight reconstructions

laws.title: Similarly built animals jump to the same height regardless of size
variables: take-off velocity or jump height per individual
body mass or length
muscle mass fraction

kingdoms.animals: jump height and take-off velocity compilations (insects, frogs, mammals, fleas, locusts, humans), Scholz and Alexander style cross-species data
kingdoms.fossils: fossil jumpers or reconstructions (salientians, fossil insects, leaping mammals) with limb and body dimensions; say plainly when thin
